content.title: KITCHEN FIXES FOR {{EVERYDAY ANNOYANCES}} NOBODY TAUGHT YOU
facts: **Hiccups** – Swallow a teaspoon of sugar; the grainy texture interrupts the nerve spasm causing the hiccup.
**Burnt tongue** – Press a spoonful of plain yogurt against the roof of your mouth to cool the tissue fast.
**Stuffy nose** – Hold a warm, damp washcloth over your nose and cheeks for 1 minute to loosen congestion.
**Bug bite itch** – Dab on a paste of baking soda and water and let it dry for 10 minutes to calm the itch.
**Brain freeze** – Press your tongue flat against the roof of your mouth to warm the area and stop the ache.
**Hangnail** – Soak your fingertip in warm olive oil for 5 minutes to soften the skin before trimming.
**Charley horse cramp** – Pull your toes toward your shin and hold for 15 seconds to force the muscle to release.
**Dry, cracked heels** – Rub a thick layer of petroleum jelly on at night and cover with socks to lock in moisture.
**Sore throat** – Gargle warm water with 1/2 tsp salt for 30 seconds to pull swelling out of irritated tissue.
**Follow along** – for more quick, kitchen-cabinet fixes like this.
content.caption:
A few of these have more going on than they look like. The sugar trick for hiccups works because the coarse texture stimulates the vagus nerve, which helps reset the diaphragm spasm causing the hiccup in the first place. For a burnt tongue, yogurt isn't just soothing because it's cold — its proteins coat the irritated taste buds, which is why it calms the sting faster than plain water. And that baking soda paste for bug bites works by neutralizing some of the acidic compounds your body releases at the bite site, which is part of what triggers the itching signal to your brain. Everyone's skin and body react a little differently, so pay attention to what actually helps yours.
